title: Appoint Elders Who Hold to the Truth
summary_text: Paul writes to Titus about faith and the hope of eternal life promised by God, who cannot lie. Titus must finish the work in Crete and appoint elders whose home lives and conduct are above blame. They must be holy and hold firmly to the word they were taught, so they can teach and correct. This matters because false teachers, especially from the circumcision group, ruin whole households for money. Paul calls for stern rebukes to restore sound faith and says these teachers deny God by their deeds, though they claim to know Him.
key_points: Paul serves as an apostle of Jesus Christ for God's elect, their faith, and the hope of His promised eternal life.
Titus must appoint elders in every town, choosing men whose families and personal conduct meet Paul's requirements.
An overseer must hold firmly to the faithful word so he can encourage sound teaching and refute opposition.
Deceptive teachers must be silenced and sternly corrected so that faith replaces myths and commands from people who reject truth.
The defiled and unbelieving have corrupt minds and consciences, and their deeds deny their claims to know God.

title: Sound Teaching and the Training of Grace
summary_text: Paul tells Titus to teach older and younger men and women to live with self-control, faith, and love. Titus must set an example in good works and sound teaching, while slaves must serve their masters with honesty. God's grace brings salvation and trains His people to reject ungodliness and live godly lives as they wait for Jesus Christ, their great God and Savior. Christ gave Himself to redeem them from lawlessness and purify a people eager to do good. Titus must teach these things, urge people on, and rebuke with authority.
key_points: Older believers must show self-control and reverence, with older women training younger women in love, purity, household care, and submission to husbands.
Titus must urge younger men toward self-control and model good works, honest teaching, and sound speech.
Slaves must submit to masters without arguing or stealing, showing trustworthy conduct that honors the teaching about God.
Grace trains believers to reject ungodliness and await the blessed hope of Jesus Christ's glorious appearance.
Christ gave Himself to redeem and purify His people for good deeds, and Titus must teach this with authority.

title: Saved by Mercy and Ready for Good
summary_text: Paul tells Titus to urge believers to obey rulers, be gentle, and do good works, since they too once lived in hatred and sin. God saved them by mercy, not their righteous deeds, through new birth and the Holy Spirit's renewal given through Jesus Christ. Justified by grace, they become heirs with hope of eternal life, and must give care to doing good. Titus must avoid useless fights about the law and reject those who divide people after two warnings. Paul then asks Titus to join him and help others on their journeys, with good works meeting real needs.
key_points: Believers must obey authorities and treat everyone gently, remembering that they too once lived in deception and hatred.
God saves by mercy through new birth and the Spirit's renewal, and those justified by grace become heirs of eternal life.
Titus must stress these truths so believers devote themselves to good deeds rather than useless quarrels.
After two warnings, Titus must reject a divisive person whose sinful conduct leaves him self-condemned.
Paul asks Titus to join him at Nicopolis, equip Zenas and Apollos, and teach useful service to meet needs.
